newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: France seeks G7-style body to oversee EMU - source.
newsitem.headline: France seeks G7-style body to oversee EMU - source.

text.p: France is seeking the development of an informal body similar to the Group of Seven (G7) rich nations to co-ordinate economic policies between countries in European monetary union, a French source said on Friday.

Like the G7, members of monetary union could meet at ministerial level or at the level of heads of state and government, the source in the French delegation to the European Union summit in Dublin said.
French President Jacques Chirac has called for a political power to counterbalance the European Central Bank after the new single currency.
France is keen to ensure that while the ECB will run monetary policy after the launch of the euro, economic and exchange rate policies will remain firmly in the hands of elected politicians.
While it initially called for a "stability council" of finance ministers inside the euro zone, Chirac has since extended the idea to include heads of state and government.

Chirac's spokeswoman Catherine Colonna said that the French president had discussed plans for stepping up economic cooperation among future members of the euro zone with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl in bilateral talks during the summit .

"The President and the Chancellor once again discussed this issue. They agree on the usefulness of intensifying economic co-operation by governments in such a way that they can carry out their responsibilities in economic policy," she told reporters.

French officials said that Chirac did not raise the idea of of a political power to oversee monetary union with France's other EU partners since it would concern only those who joined the single currency.

The idea was seek an informal grouping which would develop naturally -- very much in the same way as the G7 grew from a informal "fireside chat" to a major policy-making forum. The G7 has no formal secretariat.
